clue.text: Comes ashore with the promontory in view

parts.note: a boat or traveller that comes ashore lands
a cape is a headland or promontory jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A traveller steps onto the beach with a headland in sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in view' reads as part of the scene, but only 'view' is the definition; 'with the' and 'in' just link the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is a scenic view of countryside, or a picture of one.

clue.text: Recess in a pseudo Gothic cathedral

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the run of letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A niche found in a mock-Gothic cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'a' into 'pseudo'. 'Gothic cathedral' completes the picture: a cathedral is exactly where this recess is found.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a semicircular recess, usually at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Cleaners papers?

explanation.definitionFit: A daily is a British term for a cleaning lady who comes in each day, and dailies are also newspapers published every day.

clue.text: Ron dressed in style that's deplorable

indicators.note: Ron is clothed by the other word, so it goes inside it

parts.note: chic means stylishness, elegance
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ron wears a fashion that is frankly awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed in' puts RON inside CHIC. 'Chronic' in informal British English means very bad.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang chronic means dreadful or of very poor quality, much like deplorable.

clue.text: Shoe that lets water

explanation.definitionFit: A pump is a light slip-on shoe, and a pump is a device that raises and delivers water.

clue.text: Disease developing largely in tropical climates

definitions.text: Disease developing largely in tropical climates

parts.words: Disease developing largely in tropical climates
parts.note: reads as a disease mostly found in the tropics, but 'developing largely' also means making body parts swell to a huge size, like a jumbo

explanation.surface: A medical note on an illness common in the tropics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' seems to say 'mostly', but the disease makes limbs swell enormously, which is what gives it its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephantiasis is a parasitic tropical disease causing gross swelling of the limbs.

clue.text: Games on which to found fortunes?

definitions.text: Games on which to found fortunes?

parts.words: Games on which to found fortunes?
parts.note: 'found' looks like 'establish', as in founding a fortune, but it is also the past of find: these are games in which riches are sought and found

explanation.surface: Business ventures on which to build great wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found fortunes' suggests building wealth; the games are ones where players hunt for hidden prizes.
explanation.definitionFit: Such games are contests in which players follow clues to a hidden prize.

clue.text: A memorable observation on the St Leger, say

definitions.text: A memorable observation on the St Leger, say

parts.words: A memorable observation on the St Leger, say
parts.note: a famous saying is one meaning; the other is a comment about one of the Classics, the five great British flat races, of which the St Leger is one

explanation.surface: A racing pundit's famous quip about a big race.
explanation.walkthrough: The St Leger is one of the five Classics of British horse racing, run at Doncaster, so a comment on it is also a remark about a Classic.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known, celebrated saying is the everyday sense; the race sense is a comment about a Classic.

clue.text: Princely name we'll'11 find Nelly upset about

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the other word
Nelly is upset, so her letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A Welsh prince's name turns up when Nelly is tipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges NELLY to LLEYN, and 'about' wraps that around WELL. Llewellyn was the name of medieval Welsh princes.
explanation.definitionFit: Llywelyn (Llewellyn) the Great and Llywelyn the Last were medieval princes of Wales.

clue.text: Where running commentaries were first recorded?

definitions.text: Where running commentaries were first recorded?

parts.words: Where running commentaries were first recorded?
parts.note: suggests the birthplace of live sports broadcasting, but points to the London street that gave its name to the Runners, an early police force whose reports were logged there

explanation.surface: A trivia question about the origins of live broadcasting.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bow Street Runners were London's first professional police, based at the Bow Street magistrates' office, so 'running' records were kept there.
explanation.definitionFit: Bow Street in London housed the magistrates' court and the Runners, an early detective force.

clue.text: European getting some special appreciation

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian receives a bit of praise.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'European getting' as the definition, but 'getting' is a link word joining the definition to the wordplay; the run is speciaL APPreciation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lapp is a native of Lapland in northern Scandinavia, so a European.

clue.text: Literary AA man

parts.note: reads like a motoring patrolman from the Automobile Association, but means a writer with the initials A.A.

explanation.surface: A breakdown mechanic with a bookish side.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is Britain's Automobile Association, whose patrolmen rescue broken-down drivers; here AA are the initials of the author of Winnie-the-Pooh.
explanation.definitionFit: A. A. Milne was the English author of the Winnie-the-Pooh books.

clue.text: Shuffle for a game of chance

indicators.note: shuffling mixes things up, so these letters are rearranged, apt for a card game

explanation.surface: A dealer shuffles the pack before a gambling game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shuffle' rearranges FORA.
explanation.definitionFit: Faro is an old gambling card game in which players bet on the order cards appear.

clue.text: Point over engineers turning in, this little bird tells us

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is placed above the next

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass

indicators.note: the engineers' letters are turned round and read backwards

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
taken as written

explanation.surface: A small bird gives away a secret about some engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses RE to ER; 'over' stacks S on top of it in this down light. 'A little bird tells us' is the phrase for a secret source.
explanation.definitionFit: The serin is a small European finch, related to the canary.

clue.text: Lightly wash out 14

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of their order

parts.note: the answer to 14 down, a small finch

explanation.surface: Instructions to give something a quick wash.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue number points to the answer of 14 down, and 'out' rearranges those five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To rinse is to wash lightly with clean water.

clue.text: They're covered when we are short of rupees

parts.note: taken as written
Rs is the short form, or abbreviation, of rupees

explanation.surface: A remark about who is protected when we have run out of Indian money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of' looks like 'lacking', but it signals the abbreviation of rupees.
explanation.definitionFit: People wearing clothes, hats or coats are those who have something covering them.

clue.text: Clues about the IQ of ex-exclusive sets

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around the other

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written: intelligence quotient

explanation.surface: Hints about the intelligence of snobbish groups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts IQ inside CLUES: CL-IQ-UES.
explanation.definitionFit: Cliques are small closed groups that keep outsiders out.

clue.text: Allowing for a Latvian sort of spirit

parts.note: a Lett is a Latvian

indicators.note: sort of signals the letters of the spirit are sorted into a different order

parts.note: gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Making allowance for a kind of Baltic liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges GIN to ING, a scrambled synonym rather than letters printed in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Letting is permitting, so allowing.

clue.text: Painter in drink two-thirds of the month

indicators.note: in places the shortened month inside the drink

parts.note: gin is a drink

indicators.note: four of the six letters are kept, dropping the last two

parts.note: August is a month

explanation.surface: An artist spends most of a summer month drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two-thirds of' cuts AUGUST to AUGU, and 'in' puts that inside GIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Gauguin was a French Post-Impressionist painter known for his Tahitian works.

clue.text: Notable chemist in bygone back-street of France

parts.note: past means bygone, gone by

indicators.note: back means the French word for street is written backwards

parts.note: rue is French for street

explanation.surface: A famous scientist in an old French back alley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-street' looks like one word for an alley, but 'back' reverses RUE to EUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Pasteur was the French chemist who developed pasteurisation and vaccines.

clue.text: One with grounds for growing concern

definitions.text: One with grounds for growing concern

parts.words: One with grounds for growing concern
parts.note: sounds like someone with reason to worry more and more, but means a person whose land is used for raising crops

explanation.surface: Someone justified in becoming increasingly anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grounds' means land, not reasons, and 'growing concern' is a farming business, not mounting worry.
explanation.definitionFit: A planter owns or manages a plantation, a large farm growing crops.

clue.text: Time taken to blend a kind of whisky

indicators.note: blending mixes them, so these letters are combined in a new order

parts.note: rye is a whisky distilled from rye grain

explanation.surface: How long it takes a distiller to blend his whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blend' mixes A with RYE, a scrambled synonym rather than letters printed in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A year is a span of time, twelve months.

clue.text: Writer representing Maud's dilemma

indicators.note: a dilemma leaves Maud in a muddle, so her letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, the S included

explanation.surface: An author describing the quandary a woman named Maud is in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dilemma' rearranges MAUDS; 'representing' joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandre Dumas was the French novelist of The Three Musketeers.

clue.text: Copper about to arrest ill-feeling?

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A policeman is about to make an arrest out of spite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman and 'arrest' a police arrest, but copper is the element and to arrest an illness is to stop it.
explanation.definitionFit: To cure is to halt and remedy an illness; 'ill-feeling' is read as feeling ill.

clue.text: The shot Murphy sliced

explanation.definitionFit: A chip is a short lofted shot in golf, and a murphy is an Irish slang potato, which cut into strips makes fries.

clue.text: Sounds a tool one can count on

indicators.note: sounds means the word is to be said aloud and spelt another way

parts.note: a person who counts on, or adds up, adds

explanation.surface: Sounds like a dependable tool.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'count on' is to add, as in counting on three more, so 'one can count on' is ADDS, said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: An adze is a woodworking cutting tool with an arched blade set at right angles to the handle.

clue.text: Just the last word in fashion?

definitions.text: Just the last word in fashion?

parts.words: Just the last word in fashion?
parts.note: 'just' means exactly, and 'the last word in fashion' is the very latest style; together they describe something completely modern

explanation.surface: Simply the latest thing on the catwalk.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue splits as 'Just' meaning correct, plus the latest fashion, combining into a phrase for fully current.
explanation.definitionFit: Fully modern, with every latest development included.

clue.text: Dip rinsed with the roll of a drum

definitions.text: Dip rinsed with the roll of a drum

indicators.text: with the roll of a drum
indicators.note: the tumbling drum of a washing machine rolls the letters round into a new order

explanation.surface: Laundry dipped and rinsed, then tumbled in the machine's drum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with the roll of a drum' rearranges DIPRINSED, and the whole clue also describes laundry dried by a spinning drum.
explanation.definitionFit: Spin-dried washing has had water removed by fast rotation in a machine drum.
